title: Who Stole the Smell?

full_text:
A baker who was notorious throughout the province for his extreme stinginess noticed that townsfolk often paused outside his bakery window in the early morning simply to enjoy the delicious fragrance of fresh baking bread.

Outraged that people were enjoying his merchandise without paying, the baker posted an armed guard at his door and brought a formal lawsuit before the town magistrate, charging thirty citizens with "stealing the fragrance of fresh rye."

The magistrate, completely baffled by the absurd complaint, summoned Mulla Nasruddin to give his opinion as the resident scholar.

Nasruddin listened with grave dignity. Then he asked the baker: "How much has your bakery's fragrance diminished because these poor people inhaled it?"

"Why, it hasn't diminished at all," stammered the baker. "The street still smells just as delicious!"

"Then by the ancient law of balance," declared Nasruddin, "the defendants must pay you with an equal portion of their shadows! Tomorrow at noon, when the sun is at its zenith, all thirty citizens shall stand in front of your shop window and allow you to look at their shadows for ten minutes. If you can bake bread with their shadows, you may keep them!"

The entire town square erupted in cheers, and the baker tore down his ridiculous lawsuit in utter embarrassment.
moral: Trying to hoard what nature gives freely makes one an object of public ridicule.
